name: Trigeminal Trophic Syndrome

criteria.description: History or evidence of trigeminal nerve injury or dysfunction
Presence of painless, well-demarcated facial ulceration typically involving the ala nasi
Evidence or history of repetitive self-manipulation or scratching of affected area
Exclusion of other causes of facial ulceration such as malignancy or infection

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (trigeminal nerve lesion, characteristic facial ulceration, and self-manipulation) must be present with exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and often requires multidisciplinary evaluation

pathognomonic.symptomName: Painless, well-demarcated ulceration of the ala nasi
searchTerms: painless, clear-edged sore on nose wing

pathognomonic.symptomName: Trigeminal nerve sensory loss or anesthesia in affected area
searchTerms: loss of sensation in trigeminal nerve area
numbness or anesthesia in facial nerve region

pathognomonic.symptomName: Repetitive self-induced trauma or scratching of facial skin
searchTerms: repeated self scratching or skin trauma on face
abnormal facial sensations like tingling or burning

common.symptomName: Hypoesthesia or anesthesia in trigeminal nerve distribution
searchTerms: reduced or absent sensation in trigeminal area
numbness or loss of feeling in face

occasional.symptomName: Mild facial edema adjacent to ulcerations
searchTerms: mild swelling of face near ulcers
slight facial edema adjacent to sores

occasional.symptomName: Secondary bacterial infection of ulcerated skin
Scarring and disfigurement of nasal ala

rare.symptomName: Ipsilateral corneal anesthesia leading to keratitis
searchTerms: loss of corneal sensation with keratitis
eye surface numbness leading to inflammation

rare.symptomName: Facial muscle weakness due to adjacent nerve involvement
searchTerms: drooping face due to nerve damage

rare.symptomName: Psychiatric symptoms related to chronic disfigurement
searchTerms: depression due to chronic appearance changes

imaging: MRI or CT showing trigeminal nerve injury or post-surgical changes
No evidence of malignancy or osteomyelitis
other: Histopathology showing nonspecific ulceration without malignancy

distinguishingFeatures: Painful vesicular rash in trigeminal distribution
Progressive ulceration with raised or indurated margins
Lack of sensory loss or self-manipulation history
Ulcerations due to self-inflicted injury without trigeminal nerve lesion
Absence of sensory loss in affected area

redFlags: Rapidly progressive ulceration with systemic symptoms
Signs of secondary infection or sepsis
Neurological deficits beyond trigeminal sensory loss
references: Tucker SM. Trigeminal trophic syndrome. Arch Dermatol. 1983;119(6):484-7.
Kumar N, et al. Trigeminal trophic syndrome: a review. Neurol Sci. 2019;40(7):1387-1393.
